text:
Alex R: Hey team — urgent ask. I just had a family emergency and won't be able to cover my primary shift tonight 00:00-08:00 UTC. There's an active pager for elevated 5xxs right now (P12345). Can someone pick up primary until 08:00 UTC? Secondary is Tom H for now. Sorry for the short notice.

Incident Bot: Pager P12345 triggered (1795502440) — metric: /v1/generate 5xx rate spike (avg 7.2% over 5m). Affected customers: 2 enterprise orgs, increased error budget burn. Severity: SEV2. Linked runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/5xx-spike  | Bridge: https://zoom.redwood/bridge/P12345

Maya S: I can take primary. I’m nearby and can join the bridge in ~2m. I can cover until 07:30 UTC, then I might need to hand back unless someone extends. Taking primary + will run initial diagnostics. @Alex R hope everything's ok. :heart:

Tom H: Will stay secondary and keep an eye on alerts. If the 5xx rate keeps rising I’ll trigger the mitigation script. Please post the runbook steps in-thread so whoever is primary can follow quickly.

Leila K: If Maya needs extra time I can extend cover until 09:00 UTC, but I’d need the handoff at 07:30 so I can prep. Not in a great spot to join bridge immediately but reachable by Slack. :raised_hands:

Alex R: Thanks @Maya S and @Leila K. Quick handoff checklist I'm leaving: 1) run the health query: `curl -s https://observability.internal/api/metrics?query=service:inference.errors%7Broute:%22/v1/generate%22%7D%5Brange%3D5m%5D` 2) If 5xx > 5% for >3m, trigger fallback_model: `redwoodctl route-fallback --route /v1/generate --to-model rdl-lite-v1` 3) If latency > 1.2s open SRE ping: @eng-sre. Full runbook here: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/5xx-spike#mitigation

Maya S: On bridge. Running step 1 now. `http get https://observability.internal/api/metrics?query=...` — seeing 5xx ~7.1% and spike started around 00:02 UTC.

Tom H: I’m watching logs, tailing the gateway: ```bash
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=gateway -f --tail=200 | grep "/v1/generate" | awk '{print $9, $10}'
```

Maya S: Executed fallback to rdl-lite-v1 per runbook. Command: `redwoodctl route-fallback --route /v1/generate --to-model rdl-lite-v1 --reason "oncall emergency fallback"` — applying. Will wait 2m to check error rate.

Rotation Bot: Shift assignment updated: Maya S set primary (00:15 UTC -> 07:30 UTC). Tom H remains secondary. Alex R marked OOO.

Incident Bot: Pager P12345 update — mitigation applied: model fallback triggered at 00:18 UTC. Monitoring 5xx rate.

Maya S: 00:22 UTC update — 5xx down to 1.3% after fallback, latency stable. Noting degraded quality report may increase for a subset; notifying product: @product-ops.

Tom H: Confirmed observability dashboards show error rate trending down. Preparing scale action if we see traffic rebound. If error budget continues to be consumed >1%/10m I'll force an autoscale: ```bash
redwoodctl cluster-scale --pool inference-dedicated --replicas +2 --reason "mitigation - sudden load"
```

Incident Bot: Pager P12345 resolved at 06:12 UTC — final note: root cause suspected: autoscaler lag with burst traffic to a dedicated pool + hot KV cache miss. Mitigations applied: fallback model, forced scale, KV-prefetch job run. Postmortem assigned to eng-runtime.

Leila K: Thanks @Maya S and @Tom H. Good job. I’ll stand by in case of a follow-up handoff at 07:30 but looks like the immediate crisis is handled.

Maya S: Handing back to Alex R — I covered primary from 00:15-06:12 UTC (incident resolved) then remained monitoring until 07:30 UTC. Notes added to the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/P12345/notes. @Alex R please review when you’re back.

Alex R: Really appreciate everyone stepping in — thank you @Maya S @Tom H @Leila K. I’m back online and will review the incident notes tonight. If follow-up needed, ping me. :bow:
